title: Autonomic Modulation Through Acupuncture of Tender Points in Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS): A Pilot Study
summary:
The study investigates a complementary medicine approach to the treatment of complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) in the upper and lower limbs.
The technique used is vegetative reflex acupuncture, which involves treating specific reflex zones to influence the body’s own regulatory processes.
The aim of the study is to investigate the feasibility, acceptability and safety of this form of acupuncture in patients with CRPS. At the same time, the study aims to gather initial evidence of possible clinical effects. To this end, potential changes in pain intensity and CRPS severity are being investigated before, during and after a treatment period comprising three acupuncture sessions
conditions: Complex regional pain syndrome type I
Complex regional pain syndrome type II

interventions.name:
Patients with CRPS of the upper or lower extremities receive vegetative reflex acupuncture at specific tender points to modulate autonomic regulatory processes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Confirmed diagnosis of CRPS
2. Minimum age of 18
3. Adequate communication skills and knowledge of German (or English, if necessary)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Spinal conditions: fresh fractures, dislocations, acute trauma (< 3 months), tumours or metastases, severe scoliosis, structural deformities (e.g. ankylosing spondylitis), infections (spondylodiscitis), spinal surgery in the thoracic region, implants or fixations, cervical radiculopathy, severe osteoporosis
2. Skin: open wounds or skin infections on the pelvis, sacrum or in the upper thoracic region, severe adhesive plaster allergy
3. Severe cardiopulmonary conditions that do not permit prone positioning or pressure loading
4. Pregnancy
5. Relevant mental health disorders (e.g. borderline personality disorder with risk of self-harm, severe depression)
6. Neurological conditions (e.g. post-stroke condition, polyneuropathy, multiple sclerosis)
7. Cognitive impairments or language barriers that hinder understanding of the exercises or instructions
8. Current relevant substance abuse (e.g. alcohol, opioids)
